text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx rate observed for inference-service (prod-us-east). Alert threshold breached: 5xx >= 8% for 3m. Paging oncall.

jeff: on it. grabbing timeline from dashboards now. any customer-facing errors reported yet? pinging support.

support-sam: Support here — one customer (acct: amelia-ai) reported timeouts 10m ago. I'll flag as P1 if backend confirmed.

chris: logs look weird — very sparse traces around 15:12-15:20. dashboard shows requests present but no matching application logs for many request ids.

deepa: that smells like sampling or log-forwarder change. did anyone deploy the sampling config recently? I remember a configmap tweak in the logging helm values earlier today.

mikayla: yep, there was a deploy at 15:05 that updated observability-sampling to reduce trace sampling for inference-service to 5% (was 100%) — PR #842. It should've been scoped but the label selector was wrong and it applied to prod-us-east.

jeff: ok that's likely root cause of 'missing logs' for the affected paths. impact window ~15:05-15:20. can we temporarily bump sampling for inference-service to 100% for prod-us-east while we triage?

chris: I can patch the config now. running:

```
kubectl -n observability patch configmap observability-sampling -p '{"data":{"inference-service-prod-us-east":"100"}}'
```

chris: patch applied, restarting sampler pods to pick up config.

mikayla: restarting forwarder pods now. will enable a short debug window (5m) to capture missing fields.

alex: FYI, increasing sampling will increase ingestion — I'm watching retention limits. if it spikes we may need to throttle non-critical traces. setting autoscale triggers to be lenient for 10m.

incident-bot: NOTE: deployment detected from chris at 2026-03-15T15:22:13Z — observability-sampling patched. Annotation: emergency-rollup.

deepa: while the sampling was low, our log router dropped some TRACE payloads due to a bug in size heuristics. I have a hypothesis: sampler change reduced trace prevalence and router GC path scavenged buffers causing request logs to be dropped. need log-level evidence.

jeff: capture plan:
- collect sampler and router logs from 15:00-15:30
- rebuild timeline of request ids reported by amelia-ai
- surface any 5xx patterns by model shard / host
- confirm whether any retries/fallbacks occurred

chris: pulling sampler logs:

```
# aggregate sampler logs
kubectl -n observability logs -l app=sampler --since=40m > /tmp/sampler-logs.txt
rg "inference-service" /tmp/sampler-logs.txt | head
```

chris: sampler logs show config update at 15:05:05 and immediate sampling-rate-change ok. no obvious errors.

mikayla: router logs are noisier. grabbing the window:

```
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/router --since=40m | rg "drop|gc|buffer|inference-service" > /tmp/router-15m.txt
```

mikayla: found repeated lines: `buffer scavenged due to low activity` and `dropped trace payload size 0` around 15:07-15:18.

deepa: that aligns with hypothesis — the router GC incorrectly assumed a stale buffer and freed trace buckets when sampling dropped. That would create a gap: requests would still be processed (no application 5xx), but instrumentation missing -> alerts trigger on missing spans interpreted as failures by synthetic checks.

jeff: do we have customer request ids from amelia-ai? support-sam?

support-sam: yes — customer provided request ids: [rID: a3f1, rID: a3f2, rID: a3f9]. They map to 15:09:21, 15:11:03, 15:14:20 in our access logs.

chris: searching access logs for those ids:

```
rg "a3f1|a3f2|a3f9" /var/logs/inference/*.log
```

chris: access logs show normal 200 responses for those ids. no app-level 5xx. route latencies slightly elevated ~1200ms for a3f9.

deepa: so customer timeouts may be due to client-side retry/backoff + missing traces leading support to see errors. We should confirm if any downstream model hosts had OOMs or throttling.

mikayla: checking host metrics for shard-12 (serving a3f9): CPU spikes at 15:13, memory stable. OOMs none. I see a short GC pause on model process at 15:12:59.

alex: adding mitigation steps now:
- sampling = 100% (done)
- router GC logic patched to bypass free for N minutes after config change (temp fix)
- enable debug logs for router and sampler for 10m (already enabled)

jeff: support, please escalate Amelia-AI to engineering with notes: we saw missing instrumentation but backend returned 200s. offer credits and ask if they still see errors.

support-sam: on it. messaging customer now. ETA to customer reply ~20m.

deepa: for in-incident RCA tracking, I'm adding a short timeline here:
- 15:05:05 deploy: observability-sampling -> 5%
- 15:07-15:18 router: buffer scavenging + dropped trace payloads
- 15:09-15:14 customer observed timeouts (amelia-ai)
- 15:22 sampling patched back to 100%

chris: will attach logs to the incident ticket and mark candidate root cause as "sampling config mis-scope + router GC bug". collecting full log tarball now:

```
tar -czf /tmp/incident-2001234567-logs.tgz /tmp/sampler-logs.txt /tmp/router-15m.txt /var/logs/inference/*15*.log
```

mikayla: note for postmortem: make config change PRs require 'region-scoped' label guard and add helm test that validates label selection in prod values.

alex: also queue a follow-up to add a canary check that simulates low-sample windows and ensures router doesn't free buffers prematurely.

jeff: live status: sampling restored, debug logs enabled, router GC mitigated. monitoring for recurrence for 30m. severity set to SEV2 since customer impacted but core service not degraded.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: sampling patched at 15:22, monitoring window active until 15:52.

support-sam: Amelia-AI replied: they saw brief errors around 15:10 but service appears fine now. they accepted credit and requested RCA.

jeff: good. taking ownership of RCA. assign to deepa/chris/mikayla for write-up. cc support-sam for customer comms.

deepa: noted. will start draft with timeline, logs, hypothesized root cause, mitigation steps, and follow-ups. adding checklist for prod label guards and canary tests.

mikayla: once draft ready I'll run through mitigations and schedule a follow-up postmortem review.

chris: uploaded log tarball to incident ticket: /incidents/2001234567/attachments/incident-logs.tgz

jeff: thanks all. keep this thread updated if anything new pops. I'll handle paging handoff when my shift ends.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSE RECOMMENDATION: monitoring stable for 30m, no further customer reports. Recommend transitioning to post-incident RCA doc.
